business_patterns.top_pattern: OH PPO Local acute hospital spend concentrated at one provider
business_patterns.pattern_details: In OH, PPO Local acute hospital spend rose almost entirely at DEACONESS ILLINOIS MEDICAL CENTER. The increase reflects both more claims and materially higher paid per admission, but it is concentrated in a very small number of cases. This points to a targeted provider-level pricing or case-management issue rather than a broad market trend.
business_patterns.why_it_matters: A single-provider spike can often be addressed faster through focused claim, contract, and utilization review than through broad policy changes.
business_patterns.recommended_next_step: Run a focused provider review on DEACONESS ILLINOIS MEDICAL CENTER covering recent acute hospital claims, payment terms, and admission appropriateness for PPO Local members in OH.
business_patterns.validation_reason: The increase is highly concentrated in a small number of claims at one provider, so claim setup and payment accuracy should be confirmed before broader action.
evidence_summary: DEACONESS ILLINOIS MEDICAL CENTER drove about +$61K in OH PPO Local acute hospital spend.
The change came with 4 more claims and about +$15K higher paid per admission.
The increase accounted for virtually all of the positive change in this slice and was flagged as low baseline and highly concentrated.

business_patterns.top_pattern: VA PPO Local acute hospital spend concentrated at one provider
business_patterns.pattern_details: In VA, PPO Local acute hospital spend increased at WVU MEDICINE PRINCETON COMMUNITY HOSPITAL. The change includes more claims and higher paid per admission, again concentrated at a single provider. This suggests a focused provider economics or care-management issue rather than broad utilization growth across the state.
business_patterns.why_it_matters: Provider-concentrated cost growth creates a direct lever for contract review, claim validation, and targeted utilization management.
business_patterns.recommended_next_step: Review WVU MEDICINE PRINCETON COMMUNITY HOSPITAL acute hospital claims in VA for PPO Local members, including recent pricing, level of care, and any admission management opportunities.
business_patterns.validation_reason: The increase is concentrated at one provider and flagged as low baseline, so payment accuracy and claim classification should be confirmed before escalation.
evidence_summary: WVU MEDICINE PRINCETON COMMUNITY HOSPITAL drove about +$59K in VA PPO Local acute hospital spend.
The increase came with 7 more claims and roughly +$4.9K higher paid per admission.
This provider represented all of the positive change in this slice and was flagged as highly concentrated.

business_patterns.top_pattern: VA outpatient drug claims are landing in Not Mapped categories
business_patterns.what_is_impacting: VA outpatient drugs / OP Mgmt Oth Misc and OP IV Thrpy/Oncology
business_patterns.pattern_details: In VA, outpatient drug-related claims at WVU MEDICINE PRINCETON COMMUNITY HOSPITAL are showing up in Not Mapped categories under diagnosis Z5112 across both OP Mgmt Oth Misc and OP IV Thrpy/Oncology. Because the same diagnosis and procedure pattern appears in multiple outpatient categories, this is a gating classification issue before any utilization or reimbursement action. The business risk is that oncology and other outpatient drug spend could be misrouted or misread.
business_patterns.why_it_matters: If outpatient drug claims are misclassified, authorization routing, oncology reporting, and medical policy actions may target the wrong problem.
business_patterns.recommended_next_step: Validate category mapping, provider billing setup, and claim coding for Z5112 drug claims at WVU MEDICINE PRINCETON COMMUNITY HOSPITAL before changing UM or reimbursement policy.
business_patterns.validation_reason: Both contributing findings include Not Mapped categories and unmapped-value flags tied to a small number of claims.
evidence_summary: VA OP Mgmt Oth Misc contributed about +$42K from 3 drug claims coded as Not Mapped with diagnosis Z5112.
VA OP IV Thrpy/Oncology added about +$18K from 1 additional drug claim with the same diagnosis and Not Mapped classification.
Both findings were concentrated at WVU MEDICINE PRINCETON COMMUNITY HOSPITAL and flagged for unmapped values and small claim counts.

business_patterns.top_pattern: OH severe sepsis ventilator case created a rare inpatient cost spike
key_driver_codes: Septicemia or Severe Sepsis with Mechanical Ventilation >96 Hours
business_patterns.pattern_details: OH saw a focused inpatient Med/Surg spike tied to a single severe sepsis case with prolonged mechanical ventilation at DEACONESS ILLINOIS MEDICAL CENTER. This is not evidence of broad inpatient trend growth; it is a rare, high-cost outlier concentrated in one admission. The business action is targeted clinical and payment validation, not broad utilization intervention.
business_patterns.why_it_matters: Single catastrophic inpatient cases can materially move spend and need case-level review to separate true acuity from coding or payment issues.
business_patterns.recommended_next_step: Send this admission for case-level clinical and coding review, including diagnosis support, severity, and payment accuracy for the sepsis ventilator stay.
business_patterns.validation_reason: The pattern is driven by one high-cost admission and was flagged as low baseline and highly concentrated.
evidence_summary: One OH inpatient Med/Surg case contributed about +$59K.
The case was tied to septicemia or severe sepsis with mechanical ventilation over 96 hours and diagnosis A419.
The entire increase was concentrated at DEACONESS ILLINOIS MEDICAL CENTER and reflected about +$59K higher paid per admission.

business_patterns.top_pattern: GA inpatient behavioral health growth is concentrated in substance-use admissions
key_driver_codes: Alcohol, Drug Abuse or Dependence without Rehabilitation Therapy without MCC
business_patterns.pattern_details: GA inpatient behavioral health growth is concentrated in a narrow substance-use case mix rather than a broad expansion across diagnoses. Most of the increase sits in alcohol and opioid-related diagnoses under one behavioral health DRG, with small case counts but meaningful paid per admission. This supports a focused behavioral health utilization and care-pathway review.
business_patterns.why_it_matters: A narrow substance-use pattern often needs targeted care management and site-of-care intervention rather than general behavioral health policy changes.
business_patterns.recommended_next_step: Review recent GA inpatient behavioral health substance-use admissions for avoidable inpatient use, discharge planning opportunities, and alignment to preferred behavioral health settings.
business_patterns.validation_reason: The increase is concentrated in a few diagnoses with small claim counts and low baseline flags.
evidence_summary: GA IP BH added about +$48K, led by diagnosis F10239 at roughly +$36K.
Two additional substance-use diagnoses, F1110 and F1120, added about +$7K and +$5K.
All drivers fell under the same DRG for alcohol or drug abuse/dependence without rehabilitation therapy without MCC.

business_patterns.top_pattern: Substance-use cases are surfacing in acute settings across CA and GA
business_patterns.what_is_impacting: PPO Local / ACUTE HOSPITAL and ACUTE PSYCH
key_driver_codes: Alcohol, Drug Abuse or Dependence without Rehabilitation Therapy without MCC
business_patterns.pattern_details: Across CA and GA, a small but visible pocket of PPO Local acute-setting spend is emerging around substance-use admissions. The pattern appears in both acute hospitals and acute psych settings, with more claims and higher paid per admission, but it remains low-volume and concentrated. This is best treated as an emerging site-of-care and utilization issue, not a broad acute care trend.
business_patterns.why_it_matters: Early low-volume spikes in acute settings can become a larger utilization problem if members are not directed to the most appropriate behavioral health pathway.
business_patterns.recommended_next_step: Target UM review to recent substance-use admissions in CA and GA to confirm level of care, steer to appropriate behavioral health settings when possible, and check reimbursement consistency by setting.
business_patterns.validation_reason: The pattern is based on a small number of concentrated claims across acute settings and includes low-baseline flags.
evidence_summary: CA and GA acute hospital claims tied to the alcohol or drug abuse/dependence DRG added about +$31K.
GA acute psych added about +$17K with 3 more claims and about +$5.7K higher paid per admission.
All contributing groups were flagged as low baseline and highly concentrated.

providers: OU HEALTH UNIVERSITY OF OKLAHOMA MEDICAL CENTER

key_driver_codes: OU HEALTH UNIVERSITY OF OKLAHOMA MEDICAL CENTER
business_patterns.pattern_details: In CA, OU HEALTH UNIVERSITY OF OKLAHOMA MEDICAL CENTER shows acute hospital cost pressure that appears driven more by price per admission than by added volume. One rare vascular inpatient case also stands out, reinforcing that the change is concentrated in a small number of high-cost claims. The main business lever is claim and reimbursement review at this provider, with clinical validation for the outlier case.
business_patterns.why_it_matters: When spend rises despite fewer claims, payment terms, claim pricing, or unusually costly cases become the priority levers.
business_patterns.recommended_next_step: Audit recent CA acute hospital claims paid to OU HEALTH UNIVERSITY OF OKLAHOMA MEDICAL CENTER for rate application, claim accuracy, and the vascular inpatient case details before broader utilization action.
business_patterns.validation_reason: The operational increase is low-volume and concentrated, and the clinical driver is a single inpatient case.
evidence_summary: CA acute hospital spend at OU HEALTH UNIVERSITY OF OKLAHOMA MEDICAL CENTER rose about +$17K even though claims were down by 2.
Paid per admission increased by about +$16.6K, indicating unit-cost pressure.

business_patterns.top_pattern: CARDIAC RMS LLC activity is growing in Not Mapped categories across CA and NY
business_patterns.what_is_impacting: CARDIAC RMS LLC / Not Mapped facility and outpatient categories
business_patterns.pattern_details: CARDIAC RMS LLC is showing cost growth in CA and NY under Not Mapped facility and outpatient classifications. The claim counts increased meaningfully, while per-claim payment movement was flat to down in some views, which suggests the main issue may be provider or facility classification rather than a true unit-cost surge. This is a gating data and setup problem because it can distort site-of-care, utilization, and provider reporting.
business_patterns.why_it_matters: If provider and facility mapping is wrong, downstream authorization, site-of-care, and reimbursement actions may be aimed at the wrong category.
business_patterns.recommended_next_step: Verify CARDIAC RMS LLC provider specialty, facility assignment, and claim mapping in CA and NY before taking utilization or reimbursement action on the apparent growth.
business_patterns.validation_reason: All contributing findings include Not Mapped classifications or unmapped-value flags, and the increases are concentrated in low-baseline activity.
evidence_summary: CA OP Mgmt Oth Misc added about +$15K on 162 more claims at CARDIAC RMS LLC, while average paid per claim was slightly down.
CA Not Mapped facility activity added about +$9K on 113 more claims with only modest per-claim increase.
NY Not Mapped facility activity added about +$7K on 88 more claims, while average paid per claim decreased by about $23.

executive_summary.headline: The strongest themes are single-provider acute hospital spikes, emerging substance-use behavioral health cost pockets, and multiple Not Mapped outpatient patterns that require validation before policy action.
executive_summary.primary_business_message: OH and VA each show concentrated PPO Local acute hospital cost growth at a single provider, creating clear targets for claim, contract, and utilization review. GA and the CA/GA acute-setting patterns point to a narrow substance-use and behavioral health issue rather than broad utilization growth. Separate from those trends, VA and CARDIAC RMS LLC show meaningful Not Mapped classification issues that should be cleaned up before changing authorization or reimbursement strategy.
recommended_focus_order: Validate Not Mapped outpatient drug and provider classification issues first in VA, CA, and NY.
Address single-provider PPO Local acute hospital cost spikes in OH and VA through focused claim, contract, and UM review.
Target behavioral health and substance-use acute-setting cases in GA and CA/GA for site-of-care and care-management action.
